## #14750 Alice|999

*2020-04-25 to 2020-04-28 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/.2314750.20Alice.7C999/with/862742)*

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 17:40 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/14750
@Steve Howell This is a very small PR related to an issue you opened. A review would be nice.

**pemontto** · 2020-04-25 18:38 UTC

I made a small suggestion to update the regex to be more generic. It appears the current `^\w+\|+\d` won't prevent users setting a name `John Smith|999` because of the space

**pemontto** · 2020-04-25 18:39 UTC

Checking if the string ends with `\|+\d$` might be more robust

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 18:43 UTC

I don't think we should include the `$`.

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 18:51 UTC

And I just checked, `John Smith|99` does not break during the markdown.

**pemontto** · 2020-04-25 18:59 UTC

if you don't use the $ it will detect names like `John|99 Smith` as invalid

**pemontto** · 2020-04-25 18:59 UTC

Suggest a second test case
```python3
    def test_not_allowed_format(self) -> None:
        new_name = 'iago|72'
        self.login('iago')
        req = dict(full_name=ujson.dumps(new_name))
        result = self.client_patch('/json/users/{}'.format(self.example_user('hamlet').id), req)
        self.assert_json_error(result, 'Invalid format!')

    def test_not_allowed_format_complex(self) -> None:
        new_name = "Iago Test-O'Test|72"
        self.login('iago')
        req = dict(full_name=ujson.dumps(new_name))
        result = self.client_patch('/json/users/{}'.format(self.example_user('hamlet').id), req)
        self.assert_json_error(result, 'Invalid format!')
```

**pemontto** · 2020-04-25 19:00 UTC

Also as you won't be matching the entire string now you should use `re.search`

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 19:07 UTC

I think this should work. `re.search("\|+\d+$")`. How do you feel about this?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-04-25 19:25 UTC

That has a quadratic complexity vulnerability. Just `r"\|\d+$"` suffices. No need to check for repeated `|` when you can just match the last one.
```pycon
>>> s = "|" * 20000 + "0" * 20000 + "x"
>>> timeit(lambda: re.search(r"\|+\d+$", s), number=1)
8.713763095991453
>>> timeit(lambda: re.search(r"\|\d+$", s), number=1)
0.0036784489930141717
```
In general, it’s important to avoid regexes that match in many different ways.

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 19:29 UTC

Makes sense. I'll go ahead with the one you've suggested for now. Thanks a lot!

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-25 20:10 UTC

I've fixed it and added a few more test cases like @pemontto suggested. Thanks for all the help! :slight_smile:

**Steve Howell** · 2020-04-28 13:06 UTC

@Abhishek B Chakravarthi I  looked at the PR, and it seems fine.

**Abhishek B Chakravarthi** · 2020-04-28 13:17 UTC

Cool. Although I think a big message might look bad with the UI.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-04-28 13:27 UTC

That’s fine, it only affects a small population of folks, some of whom would potentially be trying to be malicious or playing pranks.

This is a common UI problem--we have sort of similar issues when you deactivate a user in our admin screens.  We tend to err on the side of letting the thing stick around if there's a clear reversible action (like star vs. unstar, activate vs. deactivation), and of course this technique relies on you to redraw the row with appropriate new controls.

## Recent Senders Handle topic edits #14833

*2020-05-01 to 2020-05-01 · 14 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Recent.20Senders.20Handle.20topic.20edits.20.2314833/with/866155)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-05-01 07:19 UTC

We were not handling topic edits in Recent Senders. This PR fixes the bug.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 09:33 UTC

@Aman Agrawal I just added a comment.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-05-01 09:35 UTC

@Steve Howell is there a better way to implement this function? I also use it in `Recent Topics`.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-05-01 09:36 UTC

pasting code for others:
```js
exports.get_messages_in_topic = function (stream_id, topic) {
    return message_list.all.all_messages().filter(x => {
        return x.type === 'stream' &&
               x.stream_id === stream_id &&
               x.topic === topic;
    });
};
```

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 09:38 UTC

Ideally we'd just have a proper data structure that keeps messages bucketed by stream/topic.  (We have a structure like that in `unread.js`, but it's only for unread messages.)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 09:41 UTC

Since topic changes only happen a few times a day, it's not the end of the world if we sweep through the entire messages like this, I guess.  We are sort of duplicating code that we already have in `filter.js` to filter messages, although re-using that code wouldn't really save you much here--it might actually be slightly more code to use a `Filter` object.  The one nice thing about using `filter.js` is that you automatically stay in sync with its rules about which topics equal each other (i.e. case insensitivity).

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 09:42 UTC

I guess we've never bothered to fix this in the past, since we were only using this for autocomplete?  But now we want more proper results for recent topics?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-05-01 09:43 UTC

Yeah, like list of recent senders for a topic.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-05-01 09:43 UTC

To get their avatars, A topic edit looks very ugly without this PR.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 09:44 UTC

Let's do this for now...

* make sure the topic-check is insensitive

**strifel** · 2020-09-25 22:18 UTC

@Tim Abbott 
At the moment the PR saves the value of the attribute that is set as username.
This would cause a  user with the same user name to be able to log into the same Zulip Account.
The alternative would be to use the users dn, which is unique on the same LDAP server, and normally also over multiple LDAPs.
The problem with this is that the dn can change (e.g. by moving a user to be affected by a different Group Policy in  Active Directory)

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-25 23:01 UTC

So is there no unique ID for a user that we can rely on?  Without that, I don't see how we can automatically update email addresses at all (since there's no way to know which user corresponds to which original user).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-25 23:01 UTC

I suppose that saving the DN would still work -- we can just look at whether there's a user with that DN, and if so, assume it's the same user.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-25 23:02 UTC

If the DN changes, that user gets unlinked in the LDAP integration for this purpose -- but we'd only have a problem if the email changed at the same time the DN did.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-25 23:02 UTC

(And we can document that corner case, so folks who are changing user DNs know to pay attention to that concern).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-25 23:02 UTC

I imagine it'd be correct to update the `user_profile.ldap_dn` whenever a successful LDAP authentication occurs for that email, so the "unlinking" would only be temporary.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-10-22 18:22 UTC

I suppose it could be viable with some conditionals, but the simpler story is to just have Confirmation objects, which already are where we store the date that the link was generated, be where we store the expiration details.

**Shanu** · 2020-10-23 11:24 UTC

Extending `actions.py/do_send_confirmation_email` and `confirmation/models.py/create_confirmation_link` to 
take an optional keyword argument (expiration details) could be one of the way, so now,  we can pass the invitation expiration 
details in `event` dict in `actions.py/do_invite_users`  so that ConfirmationEmailWorker can hand over it to do_send_confirmation_email->create_confirmation_link   and also queue an invitation reminder if needed. 

As for the multi-user invites, we'll be able to directly  send expiration details to create_confirmation_link.

**Shanu** · 2020-10-29 19:55 UTC

Also we could retrieve invites from `Confirmation` table (for both prereg and multi-use) to display in invitation links UI.

class SnoozeBotHandler:

        return '''
        The goal here is to have a snooze for messages, similar to the snooze function on Gmail. When you write
        @snoozebot a message for a snooze reminder x minutes, hours, days, etc. from now @snoozebot
        first replies by echoing back the requested snooze time interval. X time later, it sends a message to the
        stream pinging the users in the snooze request. I am thinking of something like @snoozebot snooze for (x) (time)
        for [list of users].   
        '''

    def handle_message(self, message: Dict[str, Any], bot_handler: Any) -> None:
        # setting up regex pattern here
        # hopefully this pattern object will work for any iteration of "snooze for x days/weeks/months...will have to test.

        pattern1 = re.compile(r"minute", re.IGNORECASE)
        content = []
        # message handling        
        if message['content'] == '':
            bot_response = "Please specify the **snooze interval** and **users** to be reminded. For help, message me with 'help.'"
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, bot_response)
        elif message['content'] == 'help':
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, self.usage())
        else:
            for x in message['content']:
                # iterate over the dictionary to check for matching patterns
                if pattern1.search(x) != None:
                    content.append(x)
                    bot_response.send_reply (message, content) 
                    emoji_name = 'alarm clock'    # type: str
                    bot_handler.react(message, emoji_name)
                else:
                    bot_handler.send_reply(message,self.usage())
        return

handler_class = SnoozeBotHandler


```

**Matt Hall** · 2020-11-30 19:39 UTC

Updated code. I'm still working on getting regex to return a string instead of a match object... doing some more reading :-)

```python3
from typing import Any, Dict
import  re

class SnoozeBotHandler:


    def usage(self) -> str:
        return '''
        The goal here is to have a snooze for messages, similar to the snooze function on Gmail. When you write
        @snoozebot a message for a snooze reminder x minutes, hours, days, etc. from now @snoozebot
        first replies by echoing back the requested snooze time interval. X time later, it sends a message to the
        stream pinging the users in the snooze request. I am thinking of something like @snoozebot snooze for (x) (time)
        for [list of users].
        '''

    def handle_message(self, message: Dict[str, Any], bot_handler: Any) -> None:
        # setting up regex pattern here
        # hopefully this pattern object will work for any iteration of "snooze for x days/weeks/months...will have to test.
        pattern1 = re.compile(r'(\bday\b)', re.IGNORECASE)
        list = []
        # message handling
        if message['content'] == '':
            bot_response = "Please specify the **snooze interval** and **users** to be reminded. For help, message me with 'help.'"
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, bot_response)
        elif message['content'] == 'help':
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, self.usage())
        else:
            if pattern1.search(message['content']) != None:
                list.append(pattern1.findall(message['content']))
                y = "Ok, I'll remind you in " + list
                bot_handler.send_reply(message, y)
                emoji_name = 'alarm clock'
                bot_handler.react(message, emoji_name)
            else:
                bot_handler.send_reply(message, "Oops, that won't work. Message me with 'help' for help on how to use me.")
        return

handler_class = SnoozeBotHandler


```

**Cyphase** · 2021-02-07 21:45 UTC

@Artmis The reason I edited the topic here was because the topic link in the topic header bar (a.k.a. the floating recipient bar, or FRB) was/is going to #637 on `zulip/zulip`, not `zulip/python-zulip-api`. This is because there are linkifiers configured on this server that automatically make text like #637 link to the appropriate place on `zulip/zulip`, and text like #P637 link to the appropriate place on `zulip/python-zulip-api`, as you can see earlier in this sentence; there are other linkifiers as well. Of course these linkifiers can be overridden in a message, as you did, but topic name links are always derived from linkifiers.

I see that you changed it back, so I wanted to explain why I did it in the first place. But I'll leave it to you now.

## Discussion on dropdown_widget #17268

*2021-02-11 to 2021-02-17 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Discussion.20on.20dropdown_widget.20.2317268/with/1116531)*

**Nishant Mittal (nishantwrp)** · 2021-02-11 18:55 UTC

Hi @Rohitt Vashishtha 

> We already support an opts.default_text parameter, why don't we just reuse that value instead of adding a new parameter?

From what I've understood default_text is used when the value is null or equal to null_value parameter. But this new parameter would display a value when the value is not null but isn't in the options either. These are two different usecases, so maybe we can have two different responses for them.

> For the end user who isn't allowed to see the private stream anyway, seeing: 'Notifications: Unknown Stream' vs 'Notifications: Disabled' isn't a huge difference.

Yup, but won't displaying Disabled denotes that the setting is disabled by the org admin? Which is not the case but it's just that the user doesn't have access to the stream. Also, using Unknown stream was suggested by @Tim Abbott  [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/16946#issuecomment-771043117).

What do you think?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2021-02-11 21:22 UTC

That's a subtle difference, yes.

Say, I join a Zulip server for the first time having never used Zulip before. Seeing the words 'unknown stream' can cause 2 things:

1. Take away from some of my confidence in the software - what software is this that doesn't have data available to it? (this can be rectified by just saying "private stream" instead of "unknown stream".
2. Leaks the (trivial) information that there exist private streams on that particular server.

Anyhow, it isn't a really big thing and we could go either way. I just want to avoid adding more one-off options to the widget.

**Nishant Mittal (nishantwrp)** · 2021-02-12 08:42 UTC

@Rohitt Vashishtha I agree with you, both ways look good, so should I refactor to display the default_value i.e. the one that is already present like you suggested?

**Nishant Mittal (nishantwrp)** · 2021-02-12 22:51 UTC

Updated the PR @Rohitt Vashishtha. PTAL!

The latter -- `git rebase --skip` is a command you can run when it presents merge conflicts to you during a rebase.

**Adam Birds** · 2021-05-06 13:43 UTC

It is, you can only have one fork. So you can then only work on one issue if using master. So you need to do this following these commands before making anymore changes

**Adam Birds** · 2021-05-06 13:46 UTC

`git checkout -b update-grafana-integration`
`git checkout master`
`git fetch upstream` - if this fails run `git remote add -f upstream https://github.com/zulip/zulip.git` first and then run again.
`git reset --hard upstream/master`
`git checkout update-grafana-integration`

Then make your changes.

Run a `git add .`
Then a `git commit --amend`
Then a `git push --force`

And then follow https://docs.github.com/en/github/collaborating-with-issues-and-pull-requests/changing-the-base-branch-of-a-pull-request to update the base branch of your pull request.

And then to get your remote master back to where it should be do:

`git checkout master`
`git push --force`

**Adam Birds** · 2021-05-06 13:47 UTC

@Adam Benesh run the above in order and you should then be straight.

**Adam Birds** · 2021-05-06 14:19 UTC

Also @Adam Benesh another reason for not doing a PR from `master` is that CI won't run in your local fork on the `master` branch, hence the changes needed above.

A few bits of feedback:
* One should always update GitHub with a comment when something is ready for a next review (ideally with notes on the changes) even if there's also a chat.zulip.org thread, since that way the GitHub state is clear if one just lands on the PR page after a search or whatnot.

## #17028 add anonymous poll

*2021-09-29 to 2021-10-04 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/.2317028.20add.20anonymous.20poll/with/1260322)*

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2021-09-29 20:53 UTC

Would be great if someone could review this PR! :smile: 
I added an anonymous poll widget (`/anonymous-poll`)) which is exactly the same as `/poll`, but without showing the names of the voters. I wanted to change as little as possible in the code so that the two commands share all the necessary code.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 23:30 UTC

This is exciting!  I'd love for folks to just try it out and post usability feedback.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 23:31 UTC

@Robert (ro-i) I am worried that I don't see significant backend changes here -- so I think the poll won't be actually anonymous, in that the API will reveal who responded in which way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 23:31 UTC

To make a truly anonymous poll work, we need the server to store which users responded, but only send to clients the number of them (not their IDs).

**Cristian Deraco** · 2021-09-30 01:13 UTC

ciao

**Robert (ro-i)** · 2021-09-30 07:01 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> @Robert (ro-i) I am worried that I don't see significant backend changes here -- so I think the poll won't be actually anonymous, in that the API will reveal who responded in which way.
@Tim Abbott Yes, I forgot to mention this yesterday night... :face_palm: That's something I would be very happy to get feedback for because I wasn't sure how to accomplish this while reusing the previous poll widget function which has been in `static/js/poll_widget.js` (moved to `static/js/poll_widget_common.js`) and the `PollData` class in `static/shared/js/poll_data.js`...

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-04 20:29 UTC

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2022-01-10 07:29 UTC

What we need to do is hide both the tooltips when the list item is removed from DOM to avoid tooltip sticking around when the list item is no longer visible. If you read `onShow` method of `do_render_buddy_list_tooltip`, you will notice we have specific code to hide that tooltip when the list item is removed from DOM. So, `onHidden` is triggered differently for both the tooltips. You should actually remove `instance.destroy()` at line 616 and call ` status_emoji_name_tooltip.destroy()` from line 565.

## #21971  review, disable send button when PM's are disabled

*2022-05-12 to 2022-05-12 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/.2321971.20.20review.2C.20disable.20send.20button.20when.20PM.27s.20are.20disabled/with/1380419)*

**Manuel Nila** · 2022-05-12 04:36 UTC

PR [#21971](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/21971) Disables the send button when a user attempts to send a private message in an org where PM's are disabled. The intention here is to give immediate feedback to the user so they don't feel betrayed after crafting a PM and attempting to send. This gives a warning as soon as they attempt to PM a user. An important note is that PM's to bots are still allowed when PMs are disabled in an org, this won't show the warning when attempting to pm a bot in an org where PM's are disabled. Feedback/review welcome and requested! :thank_you: 

(Forgive me if it's not kosher to ask for two reviews back to back, I didn't intend to work on two issues simultaneously)

## Typeahead positioning #23826

*2023-01-20 to 2023-01-27 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Typeahead.20positioning.20.2323826/with/1493624)*

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2023-01-20 18:08 UTC

@Akarsh Jain, I believe we can shorten the current description by a lot while still keeping its essence. Here's what I'd recommend changing it with:

---
9. Re-render on window resize:

We add a new event handler, resizeHandler, for `window.on('resize', ...)` that calls `this.show` to re-render the typeahead in the correct position.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2023-01-20 18:11 UTC

This, plus removing the `this.$window` part, is all I have to recommend. Over to @Tim Abbott after this. Thanks for the quick changes!

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2023-01-20 19:06 UTC

Oh, and I almost forgot about this. We would be attaching event listeners for all new instances of typeahead, and thus, adding repeated event listeners to the global window object. We should use `removeEventListener` in the `hide()` function.

Thoughts @Nehal Sharma ?

**Nehal Sharma** · 2023-01-20 20:00 UTC

Oh yes @Rohitt Vashishtha, I'd missed that. We should definitely remove the event listeners when hiding the typeahead. Maybe that also means we don't need to check for the `shown` condition before rerendering? :thinking:

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2023-01-20 20:40 UTC

No, we'd still need that check, and my assumption is wrong. We create just one typeahead object for each type: composebox, searchbox, the topic completion... But, we'd create one off ones for things like topic-editing, and that's where we would want to remove the listeners.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2023-01-20 20:40 UTC

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-02-17 14:14 UTC

@Pranav Joglekar - I went ahead an moved this message to #**code review** since it seemed a better fit and you mentioned not being sure of what stream to post on in your message.

Also, I wanted to point out that there are some linkifiers set up for referring to Github pull requests and issues. You just need the hash and the issue/PR number. So, the issue here is #24311 and the PR fix is #24382. If the issue/PR is for another repository like the mobile or terminal projects, then it's slightly different - `#M` plus number for mobile and `#T` plus the number for terminal.

Also, another stream for posts like this can be #**checkins**, where you start a topic with your name and then post updates on the issues and PRs that you're working on there, as well as what state they are in (waiting for review, blocked by x, etc.).

## #26964

*2023-10-03 to 2023-10-09 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/.2326964/with/1653137)*

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-03 09:19 UTC

Hello everyone. I've fixed a short bug here [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26964) that fixes [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/26914). I am new to a lot of technologies used in zulip and the open source scene itself, any feedback would be greatly appreciated.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-03 13:43 UTC

This looks like a decent start, Utsav, although I think a better, more reusable approach is going to be to somehow track which banners have been added to the compose box so that it’s not necessary to reach into the DOM, as you’re doing, and pluck things out before making that call to append the banners again.

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-03 13:50 UTC

I understand, is there some doc that i should be aware of that details how data is usually stored and dealt with in the zulip codebase?

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-03 13:54 UTC

I can’t think of a doc specific to this issue offhand, but if you study similar code, like that found in https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/src/compose_state.js, you might hit upon a solution to the problem you’ve taken on

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-03 14:22 UTC

okay, thank you.

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-07 17:09 UTC

Hello. I have updated the code to use a set that stores the rendered banner's HTMLElement string , before appending a new banner it runs a search for the new banner string ( since it uses .has() the time complexity is O(1) which should be sufficiently fast ) and appends to the compose banner if not present in the set already.

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-07 17:11 UTC

since different banners seem to have different properties used for rendering it seems hard to store them in a generalized container without affecting the main append function defined in the compose_banner.ts file which would end up leading to large changes.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-09 16:41 UTC

Left you feedback on GitHub, @Utsav Singh.

**Utsav Singh** · 2023-10-09 17:59 UTC

Yes I noted it. I have done both the rebase as well as the name change.
Cleaned up the commit history as well and it seems to pass all tests run.

## #26965

*2023-10-06 to 2023-10-10 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/.2326965/with/1657065)*

**Sudip Bose** · 2023-10-06 16:02 UTC

Hi guys, I've raised this pull [#26965](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26965) few days ago, currently it under `maintainer review` but no one reviewed this yet. So I was wondering if I could get a quick feedback. 
Thanks.

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-09 16:45 UTC

Left a question about how that WSL path is declared, @Sudip Bose.

**Sudip Bose** · 2023-10-10 05:58 UTC

@Karl Stolley  thank you for the review! 

I've used that path to check whether `WSL Interoperability` is enabled. Since most WSL distributions are configured to use interoperability by default, I thought this would be an appropriate path to check for. Can you please tell me, if I check for Windows-mounted disc paths like `/mnt/c/users/` or `/mnt/d/` these, whether that would be considered a constant up top for WSL distros?

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-10-10 12:55 UTC

I don’t know WSL at all. My thought was only that the less we have to maintain code to adjust for future path changes, the better. But it might not be possible. I do think that putting any path someplace more obvious is a better choice, so that a future contributor wouldn’t have to hunt down something like that inside of a function.

**Sudip Bose** · 2023-10-10 15:20 UTC

Understood. I use WSL as my development environment, and when I tested it, it worked fine. I still need input on whether I should change it or not, so I expressed my concerns in the [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26965) itself. Anyway, thanks for stopping by and helping me out. Appreciate it.

**rinwa** · 2024-02-16 12:54 UTC

Passing `oldest`, `first`, and `newest` to `then_select_id` didn't update the view.
**Research and Solution:**

After looking into this, I discovered that `final_select_id` expects a numerical value to fetch the first message.
**Explanation:**
* `target_select_id` passes `-1` to `final_select_id`.
* `final_select_id` then receives its actual value and triggers a switch statement.
* Based on the received value, `final_select_id` might assign `oldest` to the `anchor` variable.
* If `oldest` is assigned, the first message is fetched for the view.
* Similarly, passing `LARGER_THAN_MAX_MESSAGE_ID` fetches the latest message.

Created PR #29191 for #26937

Changes Made:

*2024-09-30 to 2024-10-01 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/PR.2331785/with/1951553)*

**Aman Vishwakarma (AMANVISHWAKARMA27)** · 2024-09-30 19:28 UTC

Someone please review the [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/31785).

The  [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/31785)  closes [#30025](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/30025) which required a model that selectively marks messages as read under three options:
1. Muted Topics
2. Topics I don't follow
3. All Messages

To implement it, I have approached each of the three options separately:

**All Messages: ** I directly called the `mark_all_as_read()` function .

**Topics I don't follow: ** I created a narrow `is:followed` , `negated:true` and passed it to `mark_all_as_read_with_narrow()`.

**Muted Topic: ** : At first I retrieved all the channels subscribed by the user and iterated to each, then retrieved topics corresponding to each channel as iterated and checked if the visibility policy of the topic is equal to 1 or not. If 1, I marked it as read calling the function `mark_topic_as_read()`.

## Show non-sticky recipient bar action buttons on hover.

*2024-11-08 to 2024-12-11 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Show.20non-sticky.20recipient.20bar.20action.20buttons.20on.20hover.2E/with/1978044)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2024-11-08 16:40 UTC

PR [#32233](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32233): Review Request

The pull request addresses [Issue #27265](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/27265).

### Changes in this PR:

- **Recipient Bars Hover Behavior**: Action buttons are displayed on recipient bars when hovered over, except for the sticky recipient bar, which always displays the action buttons.
- **CSS Visibility Control**: The CSS rule `visibility: hidden;` is toggled to `visibility: visible;` on hover. For sticky bars, `visibility: visible;` is applied by default to keep the action buttons visible.
- **Persistent Action Buttons with Active UI Elements**: To prevent the action buttons from disappearing when other UI elements (e.g., notification menu, topic editing UI) are active, the `:focus-within` CSS pseudo-class is used on `recipient_bar`, ensuring the buttons remain visible.
- **Conversation View Consistency**: In conversation views where a single message box is present, the action buttons are permanently visible using the `:only-child` CSS pseudo-selector for a consistent user experience.

Please review the changes and provide feedback.
Thanks!

sure, let me summarise the problem statement here: 
In the provision script which is used for onboarding developers to Zulip dev environment, we  are automatically activating the virtual env whenever a new shell is launched (by appending this command to the default shell profile) 
source /srv/zulip-py3-venv/bin/activate
This works fine for setup based on Vagrant or Droplet or WSL2, but not very desirable if the user is on a direct setup.
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/15029

And this is what the PR does: 

Added logic to conditionally write the command The `source /srv/zulip-py3-venv/bin/activate` such that it is appended to the user's shell profile only if the setup is on WSL2, Droplet or Vagrant, and not for direct dev setup.
The PR contains logic to determine if the setup is on Vagrant, or WSL2 or digital ocean droplet.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-01-11 07:35 UTC

Sure!
Some points you seem to have missed while reading commit discipline :point_down: 
> Commit messages have two parts:
>1. A **summary**, which is a brief one-line overview of the changes.
>2. A **description**, which provides further details on the changes, the motivation behind them, and why they improve the project.

>In Zulip, commit summaries have a two-part structure:
>1. A one or two word description of the part of the codebase changed by the commit.
>2. A short sentence summarizing your changes.

>Here is an [example](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/084dd216f017c32e15c1b13469bcbc928cd0bce9) of a good commit message:

> tests: Remove ignored realm_str parameter from message send test.
> 
> In commit [8181ec4](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/8181ec4b56abf598223112e7bc65ce20f3a6236b), we removed the `realm_str` as a parameter for `send_message_backend`. This removes a missed test that included this as a parameter for that endpoint/function.

> The first part of the commit summary should only be 1-2 **lower-case** words, followed by a `:`, describing what the part of the product the commit changes.


>### Commit description[](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing/commit-discipline.html#commit-description)
> The body of the commit message should explain why and how the change was made. Like a good code comment, it should provide context and motivation that will help both a reviewer now, and a developer looking at your changes a year later, understand the motivation behind your decisions.

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/df/DJottAZ4Wv3WeXaS5TD3nvr-/image.png)
Don't include lint fixes as commits.
>* It should pass tests (so test updates needed by a change should be in the same commit as the original change, not a separate “fix the tests that were broken by the last commit” commit).

## DM placeholder bug #32912 / PR #33012

*2025-01-13 to 2025-01-20 · 49 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/DM.20placeholder.20bug.20.2332912.20.2F.20PR.20.2333012/with/2039868)*

**Ritwik Patnaik** · 2025-01-13 19:57 UTC

Hello everyone,

I was working on resolving [this issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/32912), where the placeholder in the DM compose box disappears when you backspace after entering and then clearing some text. This behavior occurs because the `div` element with the `contenteditable` attribute automatically inserts a `<br>` tag when the text is removed.

I submitted a fix in [this PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/33012), which resolves the problem, but I feel there's room for improvement and am seeking suggestions for a more efficient or elegant solution.

I’d appreciate any feedback or ideas on how this can be refined further!

Thank you!

```css
    .input:has(br)::before {
        background-color: green;
      content: "No text, only <br>";
      opacity: 0.5;
    }
```
I tried to add this selector to make it work for FF
It fails when text is added after clearing the contenteditable div, causing the `::before` pseudo-element to still appear, which is not what we want.
Since we have to check whether `.input` contains a `<br>` AND it has no textnodes as children.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-01-24 01:26 UTC

**Lauryn Menard** · 2025-01-24 11:04 UTC

Ah! I think there may be some confusion around "Follow ups". When I use that in a PR comment, I mean that those are things that I think can be addressed in another PR after the current changes are merged. So in  #33101, I was noting a follow up that would happen after the changes in the PR were merged.

If I have made changes after a review in a PR, then I add a new comment in my PR that starts with "**Updates**:" and then lists out any changes that have been made since the PR was last reviewed. I usually also include any relevant screenshots of things that have changed in that updates comment.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2025-01-24 11:06 UTC

#32774 would be a good example of a PR with some of those update comments.

**Harsh Bansal** · 2025-01-24 11:07 UTC

Oh, Thanks for the clarification!

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-01-24 11:55 UTC

(replying to Apoorva Pendse)
> Instead of appending followups in the PR desc and making it huge, you can post a comment containing them.

So is this valid @Lauryn Menard?

**Lauryn Menard** · 2025-01-24 13:58 UTC

I think it's important to note the distinction between a "follow-up" and an "update". So it would have been good to clarify that in your feedback above.

An update is a change that you've made either because of review feedback or because you've changed something since the last review/post.

A follow-up is something that can be done separately from the changes in the current pull request, because they are tangental to the current changes or would be the next task to do once the current changes are completed/merged.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-01-24 14:54 UTC

**Harsh** · 2025-03-13 17:54 UTC

This is because, you're overriding the `post` with noop, instead you should try something like this so that we can invoke "success" function:
```javascript
    let payload;
    override(channel, "post", (arg) => {
        if (payload === undefined) {
            payload = arg;
        }
    });
    payload.success({
        zephyr_mirror_active: true,
        presences: {},
        msg: "",
        result: "success",
        server_timestamp: 0,
        presence_last_update_id: -1,
    });
```
after this you'll get `TypeError: padded_widget(...).update_padding is not a function` because of `buddy_list.insert_or_move`, so, just override it:
```javascript
override(buddy_list, "insert_or_move", noop);
```

**Harsh** · 2025-03-13 17:54 UTC

then you'll get **You must create a stub for $("[data-presence-indicator-user-id]").each**, for which you can add something like this... (look at `insert_one_user_into_empty_list` test)
```javascript
    $.create("[data-presence-indicator-user-id]", {
        children: [
            {
                to_$() {
                    return {
                        attr: () => 1,
                        removeClass() {
                            return this;
                        },
                        addClass: noop,
                    };
                },
            },
        ],
    });
```
now coverage for `activity.ts` should be sorted...

still you'll need to add coverage for line 179 in `activity_ui.ts`, for that you'll have to mock idle with `onActive()` as the param so that it can be called, like...
```javascript
    $(window).idle = (params) => {
        params.onActive();
    };
    activity_ui.initialize_activity();
```

No, you can try it: get the subgroups of any `can_mention_group` (which is always  `UserGroup`).

```python3
from zerver.lib.user_groups import get_recursive_subgroups

get_recursive_subgroups(group_1.can_mention_group.id)

```

Ok. I will take a look at this tommorrow.

## Document avatar URL endpoints

*2026-02-20 to 2026-02-20 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Document.20avatar.20URL.20endpoints/with/2386268)*

**Archit Sali** · 2026-02-20 08:55 UTC

I have launched an PR (#38080) on the issue (#32103):
As now Zulip exposes avatar URLs via `/avatar/{email_or_user_id}/`
and `/avatar/{email_or_user_id}/medium`, but these endpoints
are not currently documented.

They redirect to different avatar sources (uploaded avatars,
Gravatar, or static bot avatars), and follow a `-medium`
filename convention for medium-size images that clients rely on.

This PR tracks documenting these endpoints, redirect
behavior, avatar sources, sizes, and filename conventions
to align API docs with actual server behavior.

Checkout @Tim Abbott

## PR #38363: Preserve tab characters in code blocks

*2026-03-08 to 2026-03-08 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/PR.20.2338363.3A.20Preserve.20tab.20characters.20in.20code.20blocks/with/2402152)*

**23IT174 Vedant Gupta** · 2026-03-08 10:19 UTC

Hi!  @Alya Abbott @Tim Abbott👋 I opened a PR to fix #17419 ,  markdown: Preserve tab characters in code blocks․

PR: https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38363

The upstream `NormalizeWhitespace` preprocessor applies `expandtabs()` before the input is processed․ This means that tabs in fenced code blocks are converted to spaces․ This PR adds a new preprocessor, `ZulipNormalizeWhitespace`, that leaves the tab spacing unchanged, while still removing STX/ETX markers and normalizing line endings․

I've also added a test case to make sure the fix works․ Please let me know when you can․ Thank you! 🙏

*2026-03-11 to 2026-03-24 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/PR.20.2338344.3A.20Refactor.20realm_uri.20to.20realm_url/with/2405624)*

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-11 07:58 UTC

Hi everyone! ,

I'm working on issue #23380 to phase out the deprecated `uri` terminology. 

Following the approach suggested by @Tim Abbott in the issue description, I've opened **PR #38344**. In this PR, I've replaced `realm_uri` with `realm_url` across the backend tests (`zerver/tests/`) and some internal backend logic (`push_notifications.py`, `realm.py`, `auth.py`). 

I have strictly avoided touching `events.py` and `zulip.yaml` to ensure no API breakages occur at this stage. All CI checks and tests are passing successfully. 

I would be really grateful if a mentor could take a look and review it when they have some time. Please let me know if any changes are needed!

**Aadithya** · 2026-03-12 15:58 UTC

Prefer using [silent mentions](https://zulip.com/help/mention-a-user-or-group#silently-mention-a-user) when mentioning members of the core Zulip team.

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-12 17:15 UTC

Oh, my bad! Thanks for letting me know about the silent mentions, Aadithya. The time window to edit my original message has passed so I can't fix it now, but I will definitely make sure to use @_ next time! 👍

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-12 23:35 UTC

Some notifications code paths could involve an API change between the Django and Tornado processes.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-12 23:36 UTC

But sounds promising.

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-13 00:03 UTC

Thanks for reviewing this, @Tim Abbott! That's a really good point. 

I looked into it, and you're right—by renaming the variables in `push_notifications.py`, the actual dictionary payload sent from Django to the Tornado/worker processes now uses `realm_url` instead of `realm_uri`.

The CI tests are passing, so the new code handles the updated key perfectly. But to avoid breaking any notifications that might be sitting in the queue during a server upgrade, should we temporarily send *both* `realm_url` and `realm_uri` in the payload for now? Or is it safe to just do a hard switch in this PR? 

Let me know what you think is the best approach here!

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-03-23 22:29 UTC

@Sachin Kumar sorry for the slow reply, I usually don't read this channel and have been swamped. Better would probably be for the Tornado code to support reading both formats. Search for `TODO/compatibility` in the Tornado code for some examples of past transitions of this form.

**Sachin Kumar** · 2026-03-24 14:16 UTC

> Hi @Tim Abbott, thanks again for pointing me in the right direction!
> 
> I just opened a PR for the `realm_uri` -> `realm_url` transition here: [https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38637](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38637)
>

## Edit bot avatar supports upload, delete, and crop

*2026-09-01 to 2026-09-01 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/91-code-review/topic/Edit.20bot.20avatar.20supports.20upload.2C.20delete.2C.20and.20crop/with/2518206)*

**Amormio Velasquez III** · 2026-09-01 21:22 UTC

Hello, I submitted a [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/40013) for #29766: Make bot avatar upload work like other image uploads

It updates bot avatar upload behavior in the bot management modal to match user profile picture uploads: hover to upload/delete, Uppy editor cropping, and immediate save without clicking `Save changes`. Deleting the user-uploaded avatar resets the bot avatar to either the gravatar or Jdenticon. 

This [CZO thread](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/101-design/topic/editing.20bot.20avatar/near/2512161) has a discussion regarding the tooltip request in the issue, which I believe may not be necessary at this point. The bot avatar edit widget was changed to be 180 by 180 pixels to match other avatar dimensions in the management modal. 

#29766 mentioned a follow-up to implement this behavior for the "Manage user" panel which I'm willing to work on if it's still desired, I believe that issue was #34519. Also, I noticed that the issue did not mention having this specific upload, delete, crop behavior when *creating* bots.
